plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying only that second-highest bid, which guarantees non-negative profit whenever you win and maximizes expected profit overall. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses. With value $30, the optimal action is to bid exactly $30, ensuring truthful revelation and optimal expected payoff given the uniform distribution of competitors' values.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy, regardless of what others bid. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks negative profit, and bidding below reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions without changing what I'd pay if I win. With a value of $7, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $7 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only win when my value exceeds the second-highest bid, guaranteeing non-negative profit) and never miss out on profitable wins. There's no benefit to shading my bid here, unlike first-price auctions. I'll bid my true value of $36.
